question.text: At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>atm</mi></math> pressure, the enthalpy of combustion of benzene <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mn>1</mn></mfenced></math> and acetylene <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mfenced></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>3268</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>1300</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, respectively. The change in enthalpy for the reaction <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mfenced><mo>→</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mfenced></math>, is

solution.text:
Standard enthalpy of combustion is defined as the enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is completely burnt in oxygen with all the reactants and products in their standard state under standard conditions (298K and 1 bar pressure)

ΔHr=ΔHCreactant-ΔHCproduct

=3ΔHccC2H2,g-ΔHcC6H6,l

=3×-1300--3268

=-3900+3268=-632 kJ/mole
